engine_name: QDiabetes-2018 Model A (10-year type 2 diabetes risk, non-laboratory) with Indian Diabetes Risk Score (Mohan 2005, live 4-level activity mapping) and waist-to-height ratio as secondary indicators; symptom and emergency escalation layer
intended_use: Educational screening aid that estimates a visitor's 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes from self-reported, non-laboratory inputs and encourages a conversation with a clinician or an NHS Health Check where indicated. It does not diagnose diabetes, type 1 diabetes or any other condition.
eligibility: Adults aged 25 to 84 (QDiabetes-2018 derivation range; age entered as 5-year bands, midpoint used — DEC-29) without a diagnosis of diabetes. BMI is clamped to 20–40 as in the published model. Classic symptoms trigger a same-day-assessment banner; the emergency checklist suppresses the percentage and directs to urgent care (DEC-09, DEC-37). Townsend deprivation score fixed at 0 and disclosed (DEC-07).
sources: Hippisley-Cox J, Coupland C (2017). Development and validation of QDiabetes-2018 risk prediction algorithm to estimate future risk of type 2 diabetes: cohort study. BMJ 359:j5019. Model A coefficients, fractional-polynomial terms and baseline survival as published.
ClinRisk Ltd. QDiabetes-2018 open-source algorithm release (LGPL-3.0) — reference implementation used to identify the deployed engine (DEC-01).

Mohan V, Deepa R, Deepa M, Somannavar S, Datta M (2005). A simplified Indian Diabetes Risk Score for screening for undiagnosed diabetic subjects. J Assoc Physicians India 53:759–763. Points table and tiers <30 / 30–59 / ≥60 (DEC-05).

Ashwell M, Gibson S (2016). Waist-to-height ratio as an indicator of 'early health risk': simpler and more predictive than using a 'matrix' based on BMI and waist circumference. BMJ Open 6:e010159. Cut-offs 0.5 and 0.6 (DEC-06).
NHS Health Check programme: QDiabetes risk ≥ 5.6 % as the blood-test trigger — basis for the Low/Moderate boundary (DEC-04).
Diabetes UK: symptoms of diabetes (thirst, polyuria, unexplained weight loss) and when to seek urgent care — basis for the symptom and emergency layer.
limitations: QDiabetes-2018 was derived and validated in UK primary-care populations; calibration for visitors outside the UK (Sri Lanka, India) is not established and is disclosed in the methodology panel.
Townsend deprivation is fixed at 0 (a neutral average), which can under- or over-state risk for individual visitors (DEC-07).

Band labels and thresholds (5.6 / 10 / 20 %) are interpretation cut-points chosen by Lifeline Daily, classified on the unrounded percentage (DEC-04); the clinician ratifies labels and the rounding rule at HG-02.
IDRS activity points use a 4-level adaptation (0/10/20/30) of the published 3-level item; ORC-03 encodes the live mapping and is therefore a characterisation check for that item (DEC-05).
Self-reported height, weight and waist; no laboratory values (HbA1c, fasting glucose) — Model A only.

The independent R oracle (ORC-01, CRAN QDiabetes 1.0-2) has not yet been run on this machine (Docker/WSL 2 pending, OI-4); fidelity is currently evidenced by characterisation fixtures only, which prove 'unchanged', not 'correct'.
regulatory_statement: Pending clinical review (HG-02). Working position: the tool reproduces a published, openly licensed risk algorithm for general health information and screening encouragement; it does not diagnose, treat or recommend treatment, and every result screen and email states that the output is not a diagnosis and names urgent-care routes (UK 999 / NHS 111, Sri Lanka 1990, India 112 — DEC-37). It is operated as an educational/screening information service and not placed on the market as a medical device. The clinical reviewer confirms or amends this position at HG-02.
licence: QDiabetes-2018 algorithm © ClinRisk Ltd, released under LGPL-3.0; the deployed JavaScript port is Lifeline Daily's own implementation of the published equations. IDRS and WHtR are published, unlicensed scoring rules. R oracle package QDiabetes 1.0-2 is AGPL-3 (research-use disclaimer recorded in ORC-01).
